name: Thickening spray
lead: Thickening sprays are styling products applied to damp or dry hair to make strands look wider and fuller and to add volume and grip at the roots. They typically work by depositing polymers, proteins or light resins on the hair shaft, and they are aimed at fine or thinning hair. The effect is cosmetic and washes out; the products are not claimed to alter hair growth.

Thickening sprays belong to the wider family of film-forming styling products that includes hair spray. Grokipedia describes hair sprays as formulations of film-forming polymers, solvents and propellants that leave a thin adhesive layer on strands as the carrier evaporates [1]. No clinical study of thickening sprays as a class was identified.
infobox: Film-forming polymers (such as PVP or acrylates), proteins, resins, solvents [1]

paras: Thickening sprays are sold as pump or aerosol products and are applied to damp hair before blow-drying or to dry hair for texture. They are used by people with fine or thinning hair who want more apparent density. They are often used together with other camouflage products such as hair fibers, which a published patient-satisfaction study of topical fiber fillers examined [2].

Grokipedia's account of hair sprays says that polymers such as polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and acrylate copolymers form a film that sets hold and resists humidity, usually delivered in an alcohol or water carrier, with aerosol versions using propellants such as dimethyl ether [1]. In thickening products the same logic is applied to add coating thickness to each strand and friction between strands, which proponents say makes hair stand off the scalp, especially when combined with blow-drying. This general film-forming mechanism is described for hair spray as a whole; formulation details vary between brands.

Grokipedia dates resin-based hair sprays to the 1940s and the spread of aerosol packaging after the Second World War, with chlorofluorocarbon propellants replaced in later decades because of ozone concerns [1]. Volumizing and thickening variants are later marketing categories within this lineage.

Grokipedia notes that hair-spray formulations raise respiratory irritation concerns on inhalation and flammability concerns around residues, and that safety assessments of some volatile ingredients are ongoing [1]. Product build-up, stiffness, dryness and scalp reactions to fragrance or alcohol are commonly listed as possible drawbacks of styling sprays; published clinical data for thickening sprays specifically are lacking.
Archived r/tressless searches on hair fibers show that thickening and fixing products come up in discussion of camouflage routines [3].

timeline.event: Resin-based hair sprays appear, later popularised by aerosol packaging [1].
